title: The Key To Kingdom Citizenship Authority Part 1
paragraphs: But I want you to make some notes very quickly. I want to talk about rediscovering the authority of the Kingdom's citizenship. This is our theme for this year. Rediscovering the authority of the Kingdom's citizenship. This may seem strange to most people because it doesn't seem very spiritual, but I'm going to show you why this is so important. Three words we should always put together. The kingdom pertains to a country. Citizenship is a matter of status. Power is related to rights.

We will talk about this in the Kingdom of God. Our focus today in our first session in this section is, write this down. I want to talk about the principle of law-abiding citizens. Law-abiding citizens. This is a very important topic. Our focus today will be on understanding the key to the authority of Kingdom citizenship. What is the key that makes a citizen strong? I will show you where the citizens derive their power from. This includes power in the kingdom of God as well.

All kingdoms have citizens, and citizens have power if they do certain things. You can cancel your power in a country. Where do citizens derive their power from? Law-abiding citizens is a term we hear a lot. Now, let me start with something I think might help you. Our focus today will not only be on compliance with the law, but also on understanding the responsibility of citizens. Some people are happy to be citizens of a good country.

But remember that citizenship does not just mean that the government is responsible for you and provides you with privileges in the constitution. But citizenship also requires that you have a responsibility to be accountable to the government and the constitution. So it is a two-way street in citizenship. There are certain things for which you are responsible as a citizen, and you can revoke your authority as a citizen if you do not adhere to those specific principles.

I want to focus, then, on the value of citizenship first. Why is citizenship so important? Please write this down. Number one, everyone wants it. Number two, every nation possesses it. Number three, every government protects it. Every government. Number four is needed by every human being. What is this thing? Number five, what is it? It's citizenship. Everyone wants it. People travel in boats and risk their lives to change it.

People cross borders through mountains and deserts, risking their lives and cutting through fences to obtain a new nationality. They risk their children to get it. It is that important. And now, governments protect them. In this series, I will explain to you why governments protect citizens. Because citizenship is really about power. What is citizenship? It's about power. It's about power. When you grant someone citizenship, you don't just give them a piece of paper. I gave him strength.

That is why governments deal with it very cautiously. That's why you have to fight hard to get it. That's why they put you through so many procedures to get it. If you try to enter a country like America and want to become a citizen, they have strict rules. In the Bahamas, we have our own rules. In Jamaica, they have their own rules. In England, they have their own rules. Everyone has their own strict rules. Why? You cannot obtain citizenship simply by being there. They make it difficult.

However, everyone needs it. If you do not have citizenship, you cannot live your life. You do not have the legal authority to work in any country. So without citizenship, you are effectively powerless. This is extremely important. Write this down. The most powerful authority an individual can possess is citizenship. I want you to follow along with me carefully in this series. Once you obtain citizenship, you become a powerful individual. Why?

Because citizenship is the most valuable, may I use the term privilege granted by the government? The most valuable privilege a state can offer is national citizenship. Citizenship is difficult to obtain, but once you obtain it, you become powerful. Did you know that America's biggest challenge right now is not terrorists? Their biggest challenge is the American terrorist. Here you are facing major problems now. Look, you can shoot a foreign terrorist, but you can't shoot your own citizens.

They must go through due legal process. This makes it difficult because they have rights. They even have the right to attack the government and call it an individual right. They can burn the flag and call it freedom of expression. This is why it is very dangerous to grant citizenship, because once you grant it to someone, they can make claims against you and you must respect those claims. If it is within the bounds of the law. I would like you to follow up with me on this matter, please.

This year, God will put you in the right place to rediscover your citizenship in the Kingdom. It is dangerous to reveal to someone your true power, because once it is discovered, you can start making demands and the government has to respond to them. Did you know that the greatest weapon any politician possesses against the citizen is ignorance? That is why most of our politicians in the Caribbean are lawyers. Lawyers are very well known for concealing information. Not all of them, of course.

Those who are in this church never do that. I know that. Others know a lot about the law, but sometimes they only tell you enough to take advantage of you, because ignorance breeds helplessness. Listen, what you don't know is what's killing you. And most people hope you never wake up. For example, did you know that our government was hired by us? It's very simple. The word "politician" is derived from the Greek word " politis". POLITIS. Write it down. I need to remember this word in case a politician gets excited.

Just show them that's all there is to it. Bullet. Here's what it means. It means the main citizen. Write it down. The word "politician" means politics. Anyone in the government you wish to see as a citizen has the right to meet with you and you have the right to demand to do so. This is the law. But we are very ignorant. But because we are ignorant of our own strength, we believe that they are the ones who employed us. Therefore, the key to your power is knowing your position. What did you say? And you don't write that down. I am trying to show you the power I have with God. You know, Moses, excuse me, Moses was also a problem at the beginning, but Abraham was the first problem God faced. There are some things you allow the devil to do in your life because you believe he has the right to do them. But the Bible says, "Everything you declare according to my word will be fulfilled." Ibrahim knew his position. This is the first place in the Bible where the Scripture says: "And God repented." Now, wait, wait, wait. I thought that remorse was related to sin. No, regret means changing your mind. Abraham made God change his mind because he knew his constitutional rights.

And God said to Abraham: You are right. So Abraham began to bargain with God based on power. Ibrahim says: " If you found 50 good people in the city, would you destroy it?" Can you bargain with God to this extent? Yes, you can. If you know your place, see, write this down. Very important. Citizenship is the key to empowerment.

Secondly, citizenship provides legitimate access to all the rights and privileges of the state. That's why it's so strong. So, if you are a foreigner and become a citizen of the Bahamas, you automatically get everything our constitution promises you in one second. The moment you become a citizen, this is the power they give you. Access. Third, citizenship is the source of an individual's personal authority. When you are a citizen, you do not just have institutional power. Rather, it possesses individual authority.

For example, a police officer cannot enter your home because he is a citizen. You have the authority to tell him: "Stay out of my yard." " Show me the search warrant." You have this power. You can report this because you don't work for them. They work for you. Citizenship gives you personal authority. Fourth, citizenship is the embodiment of the contract between the government, the people, and the nation. It's a contract. Citizenship means that you have a legal contract to work within the context of the state with the protection of the constitution. Therefore, citizenship is the most powerful weapon you can possess. Citizenship makes the government your servant.

Citizenship makes the constitution your contract. This is why the devil wants you to be a member of a religion. Because the members do not have rights. Let's talk about this power again. Write this down. Citizenship is the legal covenant between the individual and the government. Let everyone say: a legal covenant. This is why this book is called "The Covenant". In the Bible, the word covenant is a pact that has legal consequences. A covenant is a legally binding will.

This book that you call the Bible is not a religious book. It is a legal document. That is why the Bible is called the laws of God. It is the constitution of heaven on earth. God revealed the constitution of Heaven to Earth through 66 different books, which we have collected in one library called the Bible. This book is a library of constitutional rights. If you read the book as a religious text, you will get nothing. Oh my God. Citizenship makes you a legal being.

The legal entity is dangerous because it can make claims. If you don't have a legal status, you need people to like you to get things done. What I am teaching you this year will face a lot of opposition because the devil does not want you to know your rights. He will try to do everything to fight this message of the Kingdom.
